title: ai-jail run summary
description: One document per launch, written by --run-summary. Uses only properties/type/enum/required/items. Adding an optional field keeps schema_version; removing, renaming, retyping or re-meaning one increments it.

run_id.description: 32 hex characters, shared with the --egress-log lines of the same launch

program.description: basename of the command only; null when there is none

limit.description: memory and processes come from the sandbox cgroup's counters, written only on a launch with whole-sandbox limits (--memory, --max-tasks)

status_source.description: reported: the in-sandbox wrapper's report; inferred: decoded from a 128+N exit code; direct: waitpid saw a signal; exit-code: an exit code taken as it is; none: the command never started, so no end was observed

cpu_user_ms.description: CPU time in user mode of the command and every process it left behind; processes the kernel ends after the wrapper exits (an incomplete teardown) are not counted; null when unavailable

cpu_system_ms.description: CPU time in kernel mode, same scope and the same exclusion; null when unavailable

peak_rss_kib.description: peak memory in KiB: the largest single process (peak_rss_scope largest-process), or the sandbox cgroup's memory.peak (whole-sandbox); null when unavailable

peak_rss_scope.description: whole-sandbox: the sandbox cgroup's memory.peak, every process at once (the supervisor's in-cgroup helpers and page cache included); written when whole-sandbox limits put the run in a cgroup

source.description: sandbox-wrapper: measured inside the sandbox on Linux; getrusage: on macOS, every process ai-jail waited for (the command and its own helpers), not what the command left behind; unavailable: no measurement, the figures are null; cgroup: peak_rss_kib is the sandbox cgroup's memory.peak; the CPU figures still come from the in-sandbox wrapper

denied_accesses.description: reserved: no source counts them yet

complete.description: null when teardown was not active
